correctness.rationale: All ten explicitly listed orbit-collapse families are free in order, leaving exactly the five tetrahedral orbits and f-vector (n,6n,10n,5n); exceptional cyclic overlaps n=13..24 are checked, while n>=25 follows from bounded local neighborhoods. Vertex links have icosahedral f-vector (12,30,20) and are spheres. In the infinite lift, upper/lower vertex links are five-triangle discs and a regular level has connected f-vector (21,46,27), proving S2 fibers by the PL regular-level lemma. Explicit oriented tetrahedral signs (-1)^i(1,-1,1,1,1) yield orientation-reversing unit shift. The Wang sequence then yields Z/2 torsion in H2 for odd n and free H2,H3 for even n. The actual standard-library script checks n=13..36 and independent lifted local data; finite tests only corroborate the all-order proof.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies a natural infinite family of six-regular graph power neighborhood complexes beyond known valence-four treatments, using a constructive simplicial collapse and a PL sphere-bundle identification. Its parity distinction detects integral 2-torsion and manifold orientability invisible to mod-two Betti numbers; this is a meaningful structural determination rather than arbitrary finite census or known-table recomputation.
